name: Prometheus Network Ports, Exposure and Firewall Decision Rules
purpose: Threat-aware reference; port entries are not instructions to open ports. Select relevant entries rather than loading all entries into a small model context.

default_policy.principle: A conventional port mapping never authorises opening a firewall rule.

rules.management_access: Allow management access only from explicitly authorised sources, to verified target listeners and configured ports. Reject blanket internet exposure by default; evaluate source identity, network trust, business need, strong authentication, encryption, review and recovery.
rules.threat_model: Segment home, guest, IoT, corporate workstation, management, application and backup trust zones. Private addresses and VPN membership alone do not establish trust.
rules.corporate_east_west: Deny unnecessary peer-to-peer and lateral movement paths. Allow minimum approved workload flows between network segments.
rules.home_flexibility: Home trusted-LAN exceptions may be appropriate when devices are explicitly authorised; still isolate guest/IoT networks.
rules.client_vs_server: Client initiation with stateful return traffic normally needs no new inbound allow.
rules.no_automatic_open: Entries are examples, never unconditional configuration. Verify listening sockets, assigned ports, network interface and actual need first.
rules.docker_nuance: Inspect publishing/NAT/forwarding; host INPUT rules may not govern container traffic.
rules.approval: Public administrative services and sensitive data interfaces require explicit approvals and protections.
rules.public_access_boundary: Internet-facing service exposure requires explicit user intent, scope assessment and operational approval. A service default port is never authorisation.
rules.verification_truth: Distinguish guidance, proposed action, syntax checks, actual host observations, and remotely tested reachability.
rules.connection_integrity: Before applying policy remotely, preserve an independent administrative path and prepare an appropriate verified rollback.

home_workstation.lateral: limit high-risk services to authorised hosts

public_cloud.lateral: separate public, application, data and management tiers

decision_workflow: Classify client/server role and traffic direction
Map source and target trust zones
Inspect existing firewall and middleware/NAT paths
Select narrowest authorisation or no-rule option
Validate syntax with target backend reference
Test allowed and blocked source-to-target flows
Record each exception owner, justification, approval and scheduled review or expiry
prohibited_assumptions: Default inbound deny requires explicit deny for every port
A host firewall necessarily controls published container ports

engineering_principles.problem: Determine whether a network port needs opening
engineering_principles.native_first: identify the service, determine whether it acts as a client or server, inspect listening addresses, identify authorised remote clients and establish whether the existing firewall blocks required traffic
engineering_principles.avoid_by_default: opening ports merely because an application is installed or a port number appears in documentation
engineering_principles.exceptions: inbound rules are appropriate when a required service must accept connections from authorised clients
engineering_principles.verification: confirm direction, protocol, destination port, source network, interface, listening address and successful authorised connectivity

engineering_principles.problem: Distinguish inbound from outbound network connections
engineering_principles.native_first: understand connection initiation, stateful firewall tracking and established or related return traffic
engineering_principles.avoid_by_default: opening inbound HTTPS, DNS, NTP, email or package-management ports for ordinary outbound client workloads
engineering_principles.exceptions: inbound exceptions are appropriate when the workstation itself operates the corresponding server
engineering_principles.verification: identify which endpoint initiates the connection and which endpoint listens for incoming requests

engineering_principles.native_first: use documented firewall syntax to deny unsolicited incoming connections and permit ordinary outgoing connections, while retaining only required inbound exceptions
engineering_principles.avoid_by_default: confusing individual allow or deny rules with default policies, adding redundant exceptions or assuming default deny guarantees complete isolation
engineering_principles.exceptions: different policies may be required for routers, servers, isolated networks or specialised security environments
engineering_principles.verification: inspect effective policies, ordered rules, IPv4 and IPv6 coverage, and actual traffic behaviour

engineering_principles.native_first: prefer loopback binding for local-only services, then trusted-host restrictions, trusted-subnet restrictions and authenticated VPN access before considering public exposure
engineering_principles.avoid_by_default: binding services to every interface, exposing management ports publicly or treating a trusted LAN as automatically secure
engineering_principles.exceptions: public services may require wider exposure when intentionally hosted and appropriately secured
engineering_principles.verification: inspect the effective listening address, network interfaces, firewall rules and reachability from authorised and unauthorised sources

engineering_principles.native_first: use authoritative port registries and application documentation to identify common service conventions while verifying the actual process and protocol
engineering_principles.avoid_by_default: assuming a familiar port guarantees a particular application or that a registered service is safe
engineering_principles.exceptions: applications may use custom ports, dynamic allocations, proxies or multiple protocols
engineering_principles.verification: correlate listening sockets with processes, service configuration and observed traffic

engineering_principles.native_first: keep Docker, container runtimes, local AI inference servers, databases and administrative dashboards bound to loopback or protected management networks
engineering_principles.avoid_by_default: publicly exposing unauthenticated APIs, Docker TCP 2375, database administration interfaces or unrestricted development dashboards
engineering_principles.exceptions: remote management may be justified through authenticated, encrypted and tightly restricted channels
engineering_principles.verification: confirm authentication, transport encryption, source restrictions and effective network reachability

engineering_principles.native_first: confirm that an SSH server is required, establish trusted management sources and permit only the configured SSH listening port from those sources
engineering_principles.avoid_by_default: opening SSH globally, confusing rate limiting with authentication or source restrictions, or enabling a firewall before preserving an active remote management connection
engineering_principles.exceptions: public SSH may be justified for explicitly administered systems with appropriate authentication and additional controls
engineering_principles.verification: test authorised SSH access and unauthorised connection rejection before terminating an existing administrative session

engineering_principles.problem: Understand service authentication and firewall separation
engineering_principles.native_first: treat network filtering, service authentication, authorisation and transport encryption as complementary controls
engineering_principles.avoid_by_default: assuming an open port is secure because a firewall is enabled or that a source-restricted port removes the need for authentication
engineering_principles.exceptions: some discovery or infrastructure protocols use alternative security architectures
engineering_principles.verification: independently assess reachability, authentication, authorisation, encryption and exposure

engineering_principles.native_first: inspect container port publishing, host bindings, forwarding and runtime-managed firewall rules before changing host firewall configuration
engineering_principles.avoid_by_default: assuming UFW always filters published container traffic or opening Docker daemon ports for normal container workloads
engineering_principles.exceptions: deliberately published container services may require scoped network access through appropriate runtime and firewall controls
engineering_principles.verification: test actual published-port reachability and inspect runtime-generated firewall and forwarding rules

engineering_principles.problem: Preserve network connectivity during firewall changes
engineering_principles.native_first: identify active remote sessions, required management paths and existing exceptions before applying changes
engineering_principles.avoid_by_default: enabling default-deny rules remotely without allowing management access, blindly resetting firewall rules or applying conflicting exceptions
engineering_principles.exceptions: complete isolation may be an intentional response to a confirmed security incident
engineering_principles.verification: confirm continued access, maintain a recovery path and test the effective ruleset

engineering_principles.native_first: produce only the commands necessary for the requested configuration, distinguish optional workload exceptions and present changes in dependency-safe order
engineering_principles.avoid_by_default: adding unrelated services, speculative open ports, redundant examples, unnecessary packages or commands that conflict with the stated requirements
engineering_principles.exceptions: additional explanation or controls are warranted when necessary to prevent lockout or a material security exposure
engineering_principles.verification: validate syntax, ordering, traffic direction, necessity and post-change connectivity

prohibited_assumptions: DNS lookups require opening inbound port 53.
NTP synchronisation requires opening inbound port 123.
Installing SSH automatically justifies opening port 22.
All local development servers need external accessibility.
A recognised port number proves the listening application is trustworthy.
An active firewall guarantees every service is protected.
Rate limiting is equivalent to restricting authorised source addresses.

retrieval_guidance.selection: Load rules, the relevant environment profile and only the service entries matching the task; do not inject the full catalog into the prompt.
